idea-plugin.name: dbtree
idea-plugin.description:
dbtree visualizes dbt model lineage inside JetBrains IDEs (DataSpell, PyCharm, IntelliJ IDEA), with column-level lineage powered by sqlglot.

  • Interactive model-level DAG via JCEF + React Flow
  • Column-to-column lineage tracing across CTEs, JOINs, UNIONs, window functions
  • Successor of the archived ramonvermeulen/dbt-toolkit
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.3.2

  • Smoother edges. Replaced the orthogonal / spline-based edge routing with a single cubic Bezier per edge (longer control arms, α = 0.7). The curve is now a pure function of the live source and target handle positions — dragging a model card moves the curve smoothly, and dragging back perfectly restores the original shape.
  • Over / under crossings. Each edge renders with a semi-transparent halo underneath the colour stroke. Where edges cross, later edges fade into earlier ones, giving a "rope over rope" depth cue without SVG filters.
  • Stronger selected / hover highlight. Selected and hovered cards now tint their background with the layer's own border colour (40% overlay), so the highlight stays readable when zoomed far out. Selected ring widened to a visual ~6px without shifting card layout.
  • Column prefetch. Column lists now fetch in the background as soon as the DAG appears, so the column count is populated on every card without needing to click "expand" first. Also fixes a Kotlin race where concurrent column requests were superseding each other (Expand-all was effectively broken before).
  • Edge-attach handles 3× larger so the connection points stay readable at the new wider zoom range.
  • Toolbar: shortened the title from intellij-dbtree to dbtree with the build timestamp moved below in a smaller font; the right side now shows the hover-or-selected model name (selectable for copy).
  • UX fixes: instant card selection on click (no IDE round-trip), pinch-zoom range widened to 0.05× – 4×, click no longer swallowed by 1-pixel hand jitter (drag threshold 1 → 4).

0.3.1

  • Smooth, card-avoiding edges. Model edges now follow ELK's avoid-cards orthogonal route but render with rounded corners — no more straight lines crossing through unrelated cards, and no L-bend staircases.
  • Edges stay glued to cards on drag. Previously, dragging a model card sometimes left the edge floating at the layout's predicted position. Edge endpoints now always track the live card position.

0.3.0

  • Hub-friendly layout. Layout engine swapped from dagre to ELK with layerUnzipping: a hub model with 30+ parents/children no longer stacks into a tall wall — those siblings now spread across staggered sub-columns, halving the visual height.
  • Column lineage is ~6× faster. Click-to-trace went from spawning one Python subprocess per (model, column) reached (~10-15s on deep chains) to a single subprocess that does the whole walk in-process (~2.5s with sqlglot[c], ~5s without).
  • Progressive lineage rendering. Yellow highlights now appear edge-by-edge as the sidecar finds them (debounced ~2Hz), instead of one big reveal at the end. The toolbar shows N column edges (computing…) until the walk completes.
  • Resilient to partial dbt state. Lineage still works when manifest.json is missing compiled_code/compiled_path (common after dbt parse or dbt deps) — the sidecar falls back to reading SQL files directly from target/compiled/. Also tolerant to dev/prod target schema mismatches.
  • Wider, more readable cards. Cards widened 280→320px, column names now wrap to multiple lines instead of being truncated with …, and data types right-align.
  • Race-free column clicks. Clicking a column used to occasionally show "no lineage" the first time; clicking again worked. Fixed an internal race between the open-file callback and the lineage trace.
  • Better banners. When the manifest has no compiled SQL anywhere, the toolbar now points specifically to the partial-compile scenario instead of a generic "run dbt compile" hint.
  • Sidecar timeout default raised 15s → 60s to fit single-call walks on real-world dbt projects with deep multi-hop chains. Configurable via Settings → Tools → dbtree → "Sidecar timeout".

0.1.3

  • Lazy column extraction from compiled SQL. Models without yml docs or catalog.json now show columns on demand: expand a card → dbtree spawns the bundled Python sidecar to parse the compiled SQL via sqlglot → columns appear (~1s). Extracts from explicit SELECT lists; SELECT * still requires catalog.json for source schema.
  • Better Python-missing warning. When the resolved Python interpreter lacks sqlglot, the toolbar warning now includes a copy-pasteable, path-pinned install command (e.g. /path/to/python -m pip install sqlglot) instead of generic instructions.

0.1.2

  • Fix: white-screen crash on dbt projects with non-canonical folder layouts (e.g. marts_msd/, dash/, ads_data/). The frontend now defensively falls back to a default color when an unknown layer arrives.
  • Folder name preserved on chip: `DbtModel` now carries a separate folder field (e.g. marts_msd) shown verbatim on the model card chip, while the color bucket stays in the canonical marts tier. dbt projects with namespaced subfolders no longer lose distinction in the DAG.

0.1.1

  • Auto-detect Python interpreter for column lineage — no manual configuration needed on DataSpell / PyCharm / IntelliJ + Python plugin. Resolution order: manual override → project IDE Python SDK → <project>/.venv/. Each candidate is validated with python -c "import sqlglot".
  • Warning banner in the toolbar when no usable Python interpreter is found (or when the configured one lacks sqlglot), with a clear message explaining what to fix.
  • Fix: minimap in the bottom-right corner of the DAG was rendering empty due to missing node dimensions; now correctly shows the DAG miniature.

0.1.0 — Initial release

  • Interactive model-level DAG via JCEF + React Flow + dagre
  • Column-level lineage tracing across CTEs, JOINs, UNIONs, and window functions, powered by sqlglot via a Python sidecar
  • Reads dbt manifest.json + catalog.json (real warehouse column types when available)
  • IDE theme integration (light / dark)
  • Drag-to-rearrange nodes, click model card to open file, configurable hop depth (0 / 1 / 2 / 3 / 5 / 10 / ∞)
  • Tested on DataSpell 2026.1.1; should work on any IntelliJ-based IDE on build 261+
